correctness.rationale: Single-cap coefficients are established via exact integrals for three angular orders. Frobenius-orthogonal trace-free symmetric matrices give the full five-sector spectrum for the two-cap Gram form. The xz sector is excluded from the minimum by a strict inequality on the nonoverlap domain. The smaller diagonal root and the smaller of the xy,yz offsets each strictly decrease in absolute center inner product, so feasibility uniquely forces the optimum; an explicit factor gives the sqrt(5)/3 transition and multiplicities. Every positive-radius cap interior has positive area, so no nonzero quadratic harmonic can be annihilated and inversion is stable. The independent exact-rational test reconstructs the Gram and evaluates 33 rational configurations and 19,829 grid positions, corroborative not exhaustive.

originality.rationale: The candidate is not the classical definition or computability of spherical Slepian concentration. Its claim is an exact two-cap, all-radius, full angular E-optimal theorem for the real degree-two harmonic block, a least-eigenvalue formula, and a sharp change in least-mode multiplicities. The foundational arbitrary-region paper supplies a matrix method, not the asserted closed global angular optimization; the polar-gap study fixes antipodal centers. Relevant published research comparisons did not disclose an equivalent implication. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent optimal-design results is explicit.
residual_risks: Classical spherical Slepian and spherical sensor-design literature is substantial; an unindexed or differently named exact E-optimal cap-pair theorem may predate this analysis.
The Erb–Mathias full text was not materially inspected, so its abstract cannot support a whole-paper noncoverage conclusion.
Same-model proof and numerical checks have not been independently audited.

value.rationale: The global least singular value is the exact worst-case noise-amplification invariant for stable reconstruction from spatially restricted observations. With cap area fixed, changing only their separation produces a nontrivial global optimality theorem, with a tangent-to-orthogonal design transition at rho=pi/4 and a second, rigorously characterized one-/three-/two-dimensional least-mode transition at cos rho=sqrt(5)/3. This is a natural physical and operator-theoretic design question, not a table lookup or routine numerical gain.
